browserReview: 1280x800 and 1280x720 desktop: full globe, home, Project Town, entertainment and sports navigation.
375x667 and 390x844 portrait: full globe, notebook links, expanded project reading, search/filtering, keyboard focus and no horizontal document overflow.
375x667 final globe: increased visible diameter, smaller visible numbered badges inside 44-pixel hit areas, retained professional introduction and controls.
844x390 landscape: visible footer and settings, compact left controls, Mesa book and guided walking. Selected local stop scrolls into view.
All six featured projects: three-step explanatory sketches with native controls; native and physical SoDA/Mesa selections were exercised. Art is explicitly labeled as an interactive sketch.
Nous deep-link reload: #project-nous expands the correct details and focuses project-nous. Reference filtering returns nine entries, removes the stale hash and keeps focus on the filter.
Original v4 track: user-initiated playback advances currentTime; closing the reading sheet removes the audio element. Show selection updates the selected sitcom.
Environment sound enable/mute and live/day/night selection exercised, including lighting changes with motion paused. Sound mix was not independently evaluated through calibrated audio playback.
Actual WebGL context-loss action in development: fallback appears and Try 3D again restores the scene. Later final-build 3D off/on preserves the walking clock and usable controls.
Take a walk: same world, synchronized avatar/camera, tap greeting, Enter-key greeting, short sleeves following arm motion, paused/resumed motion, portrait/landscape and exit to Project Town.
Close-up material review: walnut floor boards, desk, monitor panels, chair, upholstery, capped hair-lock roots. Artist reference fidelity remains an open review item.
